class.name: MySQLTransaction
class.brief_description: A transaction started by [method MySQLSession.begin_transaction]: [method commit] or [method rollback] it.
class.description: Returned by [method MySQLSession.begin_transaction], which already ran [code]START TRANSACTION[/code]. Run statements through the same [MySQLSession] as usual, then call [method commit] or [method rollback] to end the transaction. If every reference to this [MySQLTransaction] is dropped without either having been called, it rolls back automatically as a safety net when it is destroyed (a warning is printed). Relying on this is not a substitute for calling [method commit]/[method rollback] explicitly: it only exists to avoid leaving a transaction open by accident, for example if an early [code]return[/code] skips the intended call. [method MySQLSession.begin_transaction] never returns [code]null[/code]. If [code]START TRANSACTION[/code] fails (for example because the session is not connected), the returned transaction is already finished: [method is_ok] is [code]false[/code], [method get_error] holds the reason, [method commit] and [method rollback] return that same error, and nothing is rolled back automatically. Holds a reference to the [MySQLSession] it was created from, keeping it (and its connection) alive for as long as the transaction exists.

method.name: commit
method.description: Runs [code]COMMIT[/code]. Returns an empty [Dictionary] on success, or an error [Dictionary] (same shape as [method MySQLResult.get_error]) otherwise — including when called on a transaction that has already been committed or rolled back, or that never started (then it is the [method get_error] error).

method.name: get_error
method.description: The error [code]START TRANSACTION[/code] failed with (same shape as [method MySQLResult.get_error]), or an empty [Dictionary] if the transaction started.

method.name: is_ok
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if [code]START TRANSACTION[/code] succeeded. It stays [code]true[/code] after [method commit] or [method rollback]; check their return values for their own errors.

method.name: rollback
method.description: Runs [code]ROLLBACK[/code]. Returns an empty [Dictionary] on success, or an error [Dictionary] (same shape as [method MySQLResult.get_error]) otherwise — including when called on a transaction that has already been committed or rolled back, or that never started (then it is the [method get_error] error).
